awd_titl_txt: Conference: Semi-annual Workshop in Dynamical Systems and Related Topics at Penn State
awd_abstract_narration:
This award provides funding for participants in the “Semi-annual Workshop in Dynamical Systems and Related Topics at Penn State” for the years 2026–2028. The 2026 workshop will take place December 3–6, 2026. These meetings constitute the Penn State half of the Semi-annual Workshop in Dynamical Systems and Related Topics, co-sponsored for the past 36 years by the dynamics groups at Penn State and the University of Maryland; the Maryland half is held each spring. The workshop is devoted to recent developments in dynamical systems and to applications in related fields. Its goals are to promote the communication of mathematical results; to facilitate interaction and progress in dynamical systems and related areas; to nurture a sense of community and common purpose in these fields; and to contribute to the training of graduate students and recent Ph.D. recipients and to their integration into the dynamics community. Participation in activities supported by this award will be open to all individuals. In addition to a lodging subsidy available to all participants, conference funds will be used, to the extent possible, to reimburse travel expenses, with priority given to participants who demonstrate financial need (for example, students, early-career researchers, and those from under-resourced institutions).

Begun as a meeting place primarily for mathematicians from the northeastern United States working in dynamical systems and related topics, the workshop has, over the past twenty years, grown well beyond that scope and now regularly attracts outstanding researchers from around the world. In recent years it has featured special sessions devoted to recent achievements and current “hot” topics in the field. The 2026 workshop will include a special session on “Recent Developments in Symplectic Dynamics” and a special session in memory of Sheldon Newhouse. Themes in subsequent years will reflect current research trends in dynamics and its applications, including the classification of measures for homogeneous and non-homogeneous systems; ergodic and mixing properties of parabolic flows and sharp bounds on deviations of ergodic averages; new developments for random systems; and statistical properties of non-uniformly hyperbolic systems and their thermodynamic formalism. More information about the 2026 workshop is available at https://science.psu.edu/math/research/dynsys/workshop and the archive of the previous workshops is at  https://science.psu.edu/math/research/dynsys/archive

This award reflects NSF's statutory mission and has been deemed worthy of support through evaluation using the Foundation's intellectual merit and broader impacts review criteria.
